note: CSF 2.0 adds the GOVERN (GV) function and renames access control to PR.AA (Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control) — formerly PR.AC in CSF 1.1. Use PR.AA codes, not PR.AC.

controls.name: Organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
Risk management objectives are established and agreed
Roles, responsibilities and authorities are established and communicated
Cybersecurity policy is established and communicated
A supply chain risk management program is established
Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
Planning and due diligence are performed before entering supplier relationships
Risks posed by suppliers are understood, assessed and monitored
Inventories of software, services and systems are maintained
Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
Inventories of data and corresponding metadata are maintained
Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated and recorded
Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts are used to understand inherent risk
Identities and credentials for authorized users, services and hardware are managed
Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
Users, services and hardware are authenticated
Identity assertions are protected, conveyed and verified
Access permissions, entitlements and authorizations are managed, incorporating least privilege and separation of duties
Physical access to assets is managed, monitored and enforced
Personnel are provided security awareness and training
The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-at-rest are protected
The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-in-transit are protected
The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data-in-use are protected
Backups of data are created, protected, maintained and tested
Configuration management practices are established and applied
Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
Secure software development practices are integrated and monitored
Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
External service provider activities are monitored to find potentially adverse events
Computing hardware, software, runtime environments and their data are monitored
Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities
Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
The incident response plan is executed once an incident is declared
Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place and the root cause
Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
Incidents are contained
Incidents are eradicated
The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed
The integrity of restored assets is verified and systems are returned to normal operation
Recovery activities and progress are communicated to stakeholders
